title: Uniform provisions concerning the approval of vehicles with regard to their front and rear protective devices (bumpers, etc.)
scope_summary: Approval of a vehicle type with regard to the behaviour of its front and rear protective devices (bumpers etc.) when involved in a low-speed collision, verified by longitudinal and corner impact tests with a pendulum or moving barrier. Applies to vehicles of category M1.
scope_quote: This Regulation applies to vehicles of category M1 with regard to the behaviour of their front and rear protective devices when involved in a collision at low speed.
applies_to_components: front and rear parts of the vehicle structure affecting low-speed impact results
suspension characteristics insofar as they affect the impact test

safety-related vehicle parts that must remain functional after low-speed impact (lighting, signalling, bonnet/boot/door closing, fuel and cooling systems, exhaust, propulsion, suspension, tyres, steering, braking)
relation_to_other_regulations: Vehicle category M1 as defined in Annex 7 to the Consolidated Resolution on the Construction of Vehicles (R.E.3), TRANS/WP.29/78/Rev.1/Amend.2 as amended by Amendment 4
No replacement or alternative relationship to other UN Regulations stated in the provided text

defined_terms.label: Approval of a vehicle
defined_terms.definition: The approval of a vehicle type with regard to the behaviour of certain parts of its front and rear structure in the event of a collision at low speed.

defined_terms.label: Vehicle type
defined_terms.definition: A category of power-driven vehicles not differing in length/width and front/rear structure, dimensions, lines and materials, engine siting and weight, or suspension characteristics insofar as they affect the impact test results.

defined_terms.label: Protective devices
defined_terms.definition: Elements located at the front and rear ends of vehicles designed to allow contacts and small shocks to occur without causing serious damage (paragraph 2.1).

defined_terms.label: Unladen weight
defined_terms.definition: Weight of the vehicle in running order, unoccupied and unladen but complete with fuel, coolant, lubricant, tools and a spare wheel if provided as standard.

defined_terms.label: Laden test weight
defined_terms.definition: Unladen weight plus 75 kg per passenger, with the number and distribution of passengers set by the number of seating positions.

defined_terms.label: Vehicle corner
defined_terms.definition: The vehicle's point of contact with a tangent vertical plane making an angle of 60° with the longitudinal median plane of the vehicle.

defined_terms.label: Reference height
defined_terms.definition: Height above the ground, at unladen kerb weight and at laden test weight, at which the vehicle should embody sufficient protective devices, defined by the horizontal plane through the impactor reference line.

defined_terms.label: Reference line
defined_terms.definition: Line outside the impactor at the intersection of the horizontal plane of symmetry of the impact contour with the impact contour itself, with plane A of the impactor vertical.

classes_and_variants.name: Front protective device
classes_and_variants.distinguished_by: Location at the front end of the vehicle; tested by frontal longitudinal and corner impacts

classes_and_variants.name: Rear protective device
classes_and_variants.distinguished_by: Location at the rear end of the vehicle; tested by rearward longitudinal and corner impacts

classes_and_variants.name: Moving barrier test
classes_and_variants.distinguished_by: Impactor mounted on a moving barrier (Annex 3, 2.5)

applicability_hints: The regulation approves the M1 vehicle type, not the bumper as a separate component; a bumper, bumper beam, energy absorber or fascia is relevant only as part of a vehicle type approval.

Changes to front/rear structure, lines, materials, vehicle length/width, engine siting or weight, or suspension characteristics that affect impact results can create a new vehicle type or require extension (section 7).

Components located in the front or rear end (lamps, bonnet/boot latches, radiator/cooling system, fuel system, exhaust) may be affected because the vehicle must still function properly after the low-speed impact tests.
Protective devices must be present at the reference height at both unladen and laden test weight, so ride height and suspension changes can be relevant.
Corner zones defined at 60° to the median plane are tested, so lateral-end features of bumpers are covered.
Only category M1 vehicles are in scope; N, L and other categories are not covered.
